title: Hunting predators on fuel-driven prey cycle with them and divide: in a 256^2 arena prey 58 -> 3 -> 61 -> 10 and predators 64 -> 37 -> 45 with a lag, and predators split after meals (19 persistent splits, 21 strict); prey still divide rarely (1-2)
summary: world.py defaults (chiF 0.5, ne 2, kq 0.0015, Mb 0.005; prey as in 20261026T1851-c46-driven-prey-fuel-fork, prey matter never made from fuel; predators added as noise at t=2000). Labkit, seed 2, 256^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5 (pack256/): predators eat 58 prey bodies down to 3 by t~3800, prey re-nucleate to 61 by t~6000 while predators fall to 37, then predators rise to 45-50 and prey fall to 10 by t=12000 (pack256/timeseries.png, components per species). Predators that have eaten elongate into rods and Y-shapes that pinch into separate droplets: labkit 44 predator splits, 19 persistent (generation 2, merge/split 0.045); c43's strict test splits3.py (daughters >= 8 px and alive 500 t later) gives 21 predator splits, 14 of them away from any prey (pack256/strict_1.png). Prey divide as dumbbells only rarely: 2 persistent splits (labkit), 1 strict. At 128^2 (drive.py, seeds 2 and 3, screen128/) the same cycle runs once or twice and the prey go extinct on seed 2 at t~11300.

finding.operator: nonreciprocal fuel-depletion taxis of a Cahn-Hilliard predator with cooperative eating (k2 c_a^2 c_b^2) on fuel-driven condensate prey
finding.control: none matched yet (one 256^2 seed); predator-free prey twins are in 20261026T1851-c46-driven-prey-fuel-fork
finding.result: 256^2 seed 2: predator persistent splits 19 (generation 2), strict 21; prey persistent splits 2; prey/predator counts cycle with a lag (58/0 -> 3/64 -> 61/37 -> 10/45)

limits: One 256^2 seed; prey division too rare for D of the prey kind; no matched predator-free twin at 256^2 in this contribution; the taxis term is a written nonreciprocal drift toward low fuel. Predators are counted at threshold c_b 0.5 and dim between meals, so their tracks are short.
